The State Department released a new 100-page report titled that reveals the role Cuba has played in fostering 21st-century communism and subversion in the United States. The document breaks down how foreign governments and many extremist movements familiar to Americans, like Antifa, are helping radicalism, and its tangible effects, to grow right here on American soil.

On July 16th, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a conference on political terrorism, “the Cuban regime’s sprawling intelligence and ideological network helped to build the far left in our country and in our hemisphere, and it remains inextricably linked to the far left groups and movements across and beyond the West.”

President Donald Trump will attend the dignified transfer of American soldiers who were killed in the war with Iran. In a Truth Social post, Trump vowed to avenge their deaths, saying that the regime will pay ‘many times over.’ The U.S. enters the 9th consecutive day of strikes against Iran.

An individual is in custody after allegedly setting off an “incendiary device” at a federal building in New York City that houses Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and an immigration court, FBI Director Kash Patel wrote in an X post. The suspect allegedly poured an unknown liquid on the ground, placed fireworks on top and ignited it causing a fire, the FBI said at a press conference.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: TCD Tracker - USCRI
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: This page compiles publicly available information on third country deportations from the United States, and Asylum Cooperative Agreements (ACAs) and their impact on asylum seekers. It covers U.S. law on asylum and safe third countries, ongoing litigation, and country-specific agreements. **This tracker documents U.S. third country deportations to countries in Africa and Asia and asylum cooperative agreements across the world.**. Third country deportations are deportations of an individual to a country that is not their country of nationality or their last country of habitual residence. Since February 2025, third country deportations have been systematically pursued as an immigration enforcement tool in the United States. The United States is also deporting people with humanitarian-based protections in direct contravention to both U.S. and international law. **Taken from U.S. Soil****:**Those subject to third country deportation are individuals who have been arrested by U.S. immigration enforcement from their homes, communities, or jobs.
